bullets.title: Semis/AI trade: 5-day selloff deepens on CXMT DRAM threat & AVGO CEO warning
bullets.body: SOX logged a 4th-5th consecutive decline (down 1.8-2.7% on the day) as China's CXMT claims a 4F² DDR5 DRAM breakthrough ~2 years ahead of Samsung, pressuring MU (-4.4%), WDC (-6.5%), STX (-6.1%), SNDK (-5%) in pre-market. AVGO CEO Hock Tan separately warned AI investors have 'extreme expectations' and that capital/borrowing costs — not chips — are now the binding constraint through 2028-30, spooking the broader AI trade. Korea's KOSPI fell 5.5% overnight (-33.8% from June peaks), with Samsung/Hynix down 8-10% and Kioxia -13%.

bullets.title: NVDA: China share loss + MSFT Maia ramp cited as structural headwinds
bullets.body: NVDA's China AI chip share is falling as Huawei closes the gap under export controls, while MSFT is planning a significant rollout of proprietary Maia 300 AI inference chips — potentially 1M+ units in 2027 — explicitly to reduce NVDA dependence. Jefferies notes NVDA is also reducing HBM specs for Rubin Ultra, which could ease memory tightness in 2-3 quarters. NVDA, MU, SMCI all indicated lower in pre-market.

bullets.title: GOOGL Q3 preview: GCP expected +105-115% Y/Y; Cloud to equal Search by 2028
bullets.body: JPM previews GOOGL Q3 with Search revenue +~14% Y/Y and GCP likely +105-115% Y/Y driven by TPU sales. Cloud EBIT margins (Street ~33%) are the key focus — a beat would validate TPU economics. JPM sees GOOGL on a path to Cloud revenues equaling Search by late 2028; 2027 Capex expected $330-350B vs Street ~$305B.

bullets.title: META: Muse Wonder launch drives ~40% rally off lows; Q3 preview sets high bar
bullets.body: Meta's Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full frontier models launched with benchmark performance competitive with Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon, sending META +3.4% on the day and ~40% off recent lows. JPM previews Q3 revenue at the high end of guidance (~$64B, +26% Y/Y) but notes the stock needs concrete Muse KPIs (DAUs, downloads) plus 2027 Opex/Capex surprise to push to $800+; Street 2027 Opex at ~$203B seen as too low (most investors expect $210-225B).

bullets.title: MSFT: Maia 300 chip launch + CIO survey leadership reinforce AI platform position
bullets.body: MSFT unveiled Maia 300 AI chip for inference with 40% better power efficiency vs GPUs, with Jefferies estimating ~500K units in 2027 (below 1M+ aspirational targets). A Morgan Stanley CIO survey shows MSFT leads AI orchestration at 20% bias vs 17% for LLM providers, 5% Google, 4% Amazon; software is the fastest-growing tech spend category (+4.3% budget growth expected in 2026).

bullets.title: COHR: OW maintained; InP laser capacity is key bottleneck, take-or-pay deals in place
bullets.body: JPM maintains Overweight on COHR after PhotonLink management discussions: 400mW ELS lasers see greatest demand traction, InP lasers are most supply-constrained (followed by isolators and fiber), and multiple undisclosed customer agreements contain take-or-pay elements beyond one disclosed long-term deal. Customers are purchasing at maximum available rate; biggest challenge is expanding InP capacity over the next three years.

bullets.title: JPM raises cloud DC capex outlook to +85% in 2026, +70% in 2027; bullish on ANET, CLS, CIEN, COHR, FN, CRDO, LITE
bullets.body: JPM raises 2026 cloud DC capex forecast to +85% Y/Y ($270B+ step-up, largest in a decade) and 2027 to +70% Y/Y ($400B+). Google capex expected +120%+ Y/Y in 2026, Meta ~100%, Amazon 70%+, MSFT 55%+. Networking growth expected to outpace overall capex; JPM bullish on ANET, CLS, CIEN, COHR, CRDO, FN, LITE as capex-levered beneficiaries.

bullets.title: MRVL: Microsoft Maia XPU ramp magnitude not yet reflected in consensus — upside flag
bullets.body: Citi's OCP Day 1 takeaway highlights that Microsoft Maia is becoming the primary inference platform and the ramp magnitude is not yet fully reflected in Marvell's revenue framework, suggesting upside potential. Marvell is seen as the key beneficiary of MSFT's custom silicon deployment ramp.

bullets.title: TSM Q3 preview: N2/N3 capacity >100% utilization in 2027; capex raised to $85B/$100B
bullets.body: Jefferies raises TSM FY26/27E revenues +3% on N2/N3 demand and previews TSMC raising 2027-28 capex guidance to $85B/$100B for the next AI growth phase. N2/N3 utilization expected to exceed 100% in 2027, driving 10%+ wafer price increases. TSMC earnings Thursday pre-market are a critical read on AI demand; UBS hosting post-earnings call Oct 15.

bullets.title: NOW: Oppenheimer raises PT to $165 on solid Q3 channel checks; Security & ITOM strong
bullets.body: Oppenheimer raises NOW PT to $165 (from $140), modeling 3Q revenue $4.09B (+20% Y/Y) and adj EPS $1.08, with upside to 2026 AI ACV guidance. Channel checks point to solid demand across Security, ITOM, and new pricing tiers gaining traction; headwinds from softer federal spending and AI ROI scrutiny may lengthen sales cycles.

bullets.title: ADBE: HSBC downgrades to Hold, cuts PT to $267 on AI clone competitive threat
bullets.body: HSBC downgraded ADBE from Buy to Hold, cutting the PT to $267 from $310 (12% upside from $238), citing reports of 'vibe coded' Adobe clones as a competitive pressure. FactSet consensus PT is $269.50 with a range of $195-$373.

bullets.title: CIFR: $850M convertible notes deal to fund 3.4 GW HPC pipeline and Barber Lake project
bullets.body: Cipher Digital (CIFR) launched an $850M convertible senior notes offering (plus $150M greenshoe) due November 2032 with 0% coupon and 35-45% conversion premium, with Morgan Stanley as lead left bookrunner. Proceeds earmarked for the Barber Lake project equity investment and accelerating a 3.4 GW HPC pipeline buildout.

bullets.title: HUT/WULF/BTDR/CORZ: Power-scarcity theme; HUT and WULF in top picks, BTDR/CORZ less attractive
bullets.body: A research note on AI-driven powered shells flags 5.9 GW contracted HPC and 38 GW+ pipeline across the sector, with shares down ~27% avg over the past 3 months. HUT and APLD/CIFR rank as top picks on location, funding costs, and execution; BTDR faces Ohio regulatory and litigation headwinds with weak DCF support; CORZ screens less attractively. WULF moving to AI-friendly Kentucky. Most names trade below DCF on contracted ops with minimal pipeline value priced in.

bullets.title: TSEM: SiGe partnership expansion with Semtech is multi-year, multi-fab capacity deal
bullets.body: Tower Semiconductor and Semtech announced an expanded multi-year SiGe capacity agreement spanning TSEM's US, Israel, and Japan fabs, building on a 20-year partnership. Semtech will invest in dedicated SiGe capacity to support growing AI data center optical interconnect demand; TSEM shares up 3.0% in pre-market.

bullets.title: APP: JPM flags cautious stance — growth deceleration and Unity competition risks
bullets.body: JPM's 'cautious names' list flags APP for growth deceleration risk as model optimization initiatives have been pushed out, Unity's Vector platform threatens mobile user acquisition spend share, and retail media expansion faces competition from larger platforms with take-rate compression risk.

bullets.title: DKNG: NFL Week 5 average hold week; UBS maintains Buy
bullets.body: UBS notes NFL Week 5 (as of Oct 12) was an average hold week for sportsbooks, with 9 of 15 favorites winning (60% vs. typical 75%+). DKNG expects normal hold when 3-4 of 5 biggest favorites win; 4 of the 5 biggest moneyline favorites did win. UBS maintains Buy.

bullets.title: AMD: FermiI data center credit support deal expands partnership to 650 MW
bullets.body: FRMI signed a credit support agreement with AMD for the 222 MW gross-power Project Matador Phase 1 in Carson County, Texas, representing a key milestone toward project financing. The two also signed a partnership framework for future expansion up to 650 MW gross capacity, with Phase 1 generating ~$6.5B total contracted revenue and beginning H2 2027.

bullets.title: AFRM/LYV/SPHR: Goldman PT cuts on fintech rate headwinds; LYV remains Buy
bullets.body: Goldman cuts AFRM PT to $103, SOFI to $15, UPST to $28, and KLAR to $18 citing higher rates headwinds on fintech. LYV remains Buy with 2026+ estimates raised ~1% on Venue Nation expansion. SPHR PT cut to $170 from $189 on weaker Wizard of Oz performance with 2026/27 AOI down 6-10%.

bullets.title: NFLX: Reports Tue Oct 20 after close; also secured exclusive FIFA World Cup 2030 rights in Spain
bullets.body: Netflix earnings are scheduled for Tuesday October 20 after close, with consensus at $0.82 EPS and $12.87B revenue. NFLX also secured exclusive FIFA World Cup 2030 broadcast rights in Spain, per Jefferies, though Piper's teen survey flags YouTube time-spent increases as a negative signal for NFLX.

bullets.title: DIS: Stalking horse bid for Character.ai IP in Chapter 11 bankruptcy at $20M
bullets.body: Character.ai filed voluntary Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Delaware; Disney will serve as stalking horse bidder for a non-exclusive perpetual license of Character.ai's IP for $20M plus transition services using hired former Character.ai employees. Sale process completion expected late November or early December 2026.
